name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 6 points on the PVI
Salinas has a massive fundraising edge ($1.6M vs ~$13K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Andrea Salinas is an incumbent in a district that leans Democratic, and she has out-raised David Russ by more than 100-to-1 with no outside opposition spending against her. Markets price her at roughly 97%, consistent with fundamentals pointing to a comfortable double-digit margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's 6th District is a first-term Democratic-held seat with a six-point Democratic lean. Incumbent Andrea Salinas is running for reelection and has built a substantial financial advantage, raising about $1.6 million with $611,000 on hand, while Republican David Russ has raised roughly $13,000 and has no outside spending on either side.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Salinas around 97% to win. Everything points to a safe Democratic hold with a double-digit expected margin, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of polling.
